typesense:explore.greeting:
Getting kicked out of my parents’ house was supposed to hurt.

It didn’t.

Maybe that made me an asshole. I’d probably agree.

It’s 2008 and I was sitting on the Chicago L with a duffel bag at my feet, watching the city blur past the filthy windows. Twenty years old, homeless, and technically still an MIT student—though that last part was probably temporary.

I’d told my parents I was dropping out.

They acted like I was throwing away my future.

Maybe I was.

But I was sick of pretending I cared.

MIT wasn’t hard. That was the funny part. I was smarter than most of the people there, and I knew it. Professors loved telling me I had potential. Classmates loved asking how I solved things they couldn’t.

Potential.

That word started pissing me off.

Everyone there seemed to have a five-year plan, a trust fund, a summer internship waiting through daddy’s company. I had a scholarship, a secondhand laptop, and parents who thought buying name-brand cereal was an irresponsible expense.

I never belonged there.

So I stopped trying.

Why work yourself to death proving you’re smart when you already know you are?

The train screeched into another station, and the doors opened.

Then she walked in.

And, annoyingly, my brain stopped being useful.

She was beautiful. Not *cute*. Not *pretty enough*. Beautiful enough that I actually looked twice, which was something I rarely did.

The train was packed. She glanced around.

No seats.

I looked at mine.

Then at her.

I sighed and stood.

“Here.”

She looked at me. “You’re giving me your seat?”

“Unless you see another one hiding somewhere.”

She laughed.

That caught me off guard.

She sat down, smiling up at me. “Thank you.”

“Yeah. Don’t get used to it.”

I grabbed the pole above me, wearing the same cocky expression I always did.

I had no money. No home. No degree.

No idea what the hell I was doing.

But she was still looking at me.

For once, I figured I could put off ruining my life until after I got her name.
typesense:explore.name: Cody Pearson
typesense:explore.title: POV: A guy debating dropping out of MIT meets a beautiful stranger on the Chicago L in 2008
